title: Vietnamese Iced Coffee (Cà Phê Sữa Đá) with a Phin
summary: Strong dark-roast coffee dripped slowly through a phin onto sweetened condensed milk, stirred and poured over ice for a rich, sweet, bittersweet iced coffee.

ingredients.item: dark-roast ground coffee, medium-fine (Vietnamese-style blend if you can)

steps.title: Ready the glass
steps.text: Spoon the condensed milk into the heatproof glass and set the phin plate and chamber on top.

steps.title: Load
steps.text: Add the coffee to the chamber, shake it level and rest the press screen on top with only light pressure. Pressing hard packs the coffee and stops the drip.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.text: Pour in about 20 ml of the hot water, just enough to wet the grounds, and wait 1 minute while they swell and darken. This lets the coffee brew evenly.

steps.title: Drip
steps.text: Fill the chamber with the remaining water, cover and let it drip slowly, 4-6 minutes. If it stops, loosen the screen a quarter turn; if it runs through in under 3 minutes, use a finer grind next time.

steps.title: Stir and pour
steps.text: Lift off the phin and stir the dark coffee into the condensed milk until it is caramel-coloured. Pour it over the glass of ice and stir again.

tips: A medium-fine grind, a little coarser than for espresso, gives the right slow drip.
Pour the coffee over ice only after it is mixed with the milk, so the condensed milk dissolves.
Add an extra tablespoon of condensed milk for a sweeter café-style glass.
storage: Best made fresh. Brewed coffee can be chilled for up to 1 day and poured over ice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
